entities.summary: Cristóbal de Morales (1500–1553), a Spanish composer of the Renaissance, is generally regarded as the most influential Spanish composer before Tomás Luis de Victoria. Born in Seville, Morales studied music at the Cathedral School in Seville and later in Rome, where he was exposed to the works of Palestrina. In 1530, he was appointed as the maestro de capilla (master of the chapel) at the Cathedral of Seville, a position he held until his death in 1553. During his tenure, Morales composed a number of works, including masses, motets, and secular music. His compositions were characterized by their use of complex polyphony and innovative use of instruments, such as the lute and the organ. Morales' music had a significant impact on the development of Spanish music and influenced later composers, including Victoria. The Cathedral of Seville still maintains a collection of his compositions, which are considered some of the finest examples of Spanish Renaissance music. Morales' legacy extends beyond his own music, as his compositions reflect the cultural and artistic achievements of the Renaissance in Spain.
